newsitem.title: MEXICO: Three anti-drug agents gunned down in Mexico City.
newsitem.headline: Three anti-drug agents gunned down in Mexico City.

text.p: Three anti-drug agents, including a top justice official from the Mexican border state of Baja California, were gunned down on Saturday as they left Mexico City airport, authorities said.

The attorney general's office said in a statement that unknown gunmen shot dead Ernesto Ibarra Santes, a senior commander of the Federal Judicial Police in the northern city of Tijuana, and two of his agents as they travelled in an airport taxi. The taxi driver was also killed.

"First Commander Ibarra Santes had participated in anti-drug operations aimed chiefly against the Arellano Felix brothers," the statement said, referring to the three brothers believed to head the so-called Tijuana cartel -- one of Mexico's most violent drug gangs.
Just two days before the slayings, police seized four properties they said belonged to the Arellano Felix brothers in Tijuana, and found 76 kilograms of cocaine.
"The attorney general's office will not rest and will redouble its efforts to capture the Arellano Felix brothers," the statement said.
It added that Ibarra Santes was also involved in the capture of the Lupercio Serratos brothers, alleged heads of the Jalisco cartel, in August.
